## Amendment 3: information release stops both comparisons

**Larger dielectric branch: inconclusive. Smaller dielectric branch: inconclusive under the 10% non-Kiepe improvement / at-most-1% common-149 increase rule.** The [retained larger source/seed A information calculation](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/amendment-3/information-results.json) fails the complete-system conditioning requirement before any fit. All four treatment/control fits remain unrun. The [full report](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/amendment-3/README.md) preserves the fixed stage-2 CO₂–water law, 16-coordinate treatment, 14-coordinate control and all 205 positive-weight observations.

| Weighted, scaled information block at the larger start | Rank / columns | Condition | Release requirement |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Existing nuisance directions, all free | 14 / 14 | 6390.086918958839 | Pass, ≤10000 |
| New CO₂–MEA pair projected against all nuisance directions | 2 / 2 | 6.298512700977455 | Pass, rank 2 and ≤10000 |
| Complete free set | 16 / 16 | 562848.8359854996 | **Fail, >10000** |

All 217 information observations are Available, including twelve loaded-density requests with zero objective weight. The projected pair is distinguishable locally by rank, while the complete 16-column system fails its separate information threshold. These statements use the declared optimizer scales and 10⁻¹⁴ relative singular cutoff. No rescaling, dropped slope, fixed nuisance coordinate or changed tolerance was used. The native exception's generic wording blames the mandatory block; its own report shows that block passes and the complete-system condition fails. No other start or fit follows this hard stop.

At this larger start, all 39 Kiepe rows pass [fixed-binary invariance](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/amendment-3/larger-dV-start-Kiepe.csv) against the same-wheel qualified reference: maximum $|r_{K,new}-r_{K,reference}|=1.3785847463587686\times10^{-14}$, with $r_K=\ln(P_{calc}/P_{obs})/\sqrt{39}$. Both new weighted optimizer derivatives are zero on every Kiepe row. The two limits remain 10⁻⁸ in weighted-row and weighted-derivative units, respectively; neither is in Pa. This is a start check, not endpoint replay.

The source/seed A values give **C₂₀₅=195.70428763022872, C₁₆₆=195.70360861073 and C₁₄₉=159.6463713717262**, with the CO₂–MEA pair still (0, 0 K) and no active start bound. The [costs by family](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/amendment-3/larger-dV-start-family-costs.csv) retain every contribution. At 7 mol MEA/kg water and 101325 Pa, the four [seed Cp predictions](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/amendment-3/larger-dV-start-Cp.csv) are 3.8429337814983437, 3.4007092926258196, 3.8315431506913087 and 3.3338543689118705 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, with signed errors +3.3185584486716824%, +0.9861705308335411%, −0.6497134602678645% and −3.942882735129205%. Ordering is 318.15 K/loadings 0 and 0.358, then 353.15 K/loadings 0 and 0.358; nominal zero uses the declared 10⁻⁶ carbon proxy and complete-feed mass conversion. These values are seed diagnostics, not fitted endpoints.

For each of the four fits, convergence/iterations, C₁₆₆ and C₁₄₉, endpoint Kiepe invariance, fitted active bounds, fitted CO₂–MEA values and fitted Cp errors are unavailable. Controls declare CO₂–MEA fixed at (0, 0 K); treatments start there. Centered derivative re-solves, serialized start/endpoint cold replay, raw closure and subsequent assessments remain unrun. A complete bound-active control would complete its comparison and remain unadopted; that exception does not remove this earlier information stop. A compact table communicates these scalar release quantities; no fitted-comparison figure has endpoints to display.

The [resumed ledger](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/amendment-3/resume-accounting.json) applies all three supplied orchestrator decisions: bounded 60 s post-termination grace and own-PID kill/reap, the recorded ledger as the admission basis despite unknowable earlier overhead, and historical idle time excluded from active wall. Prior active charge is **15124.735403 − 5215.0172 = 9909.718203 s**, including the earlier preparation/reporting charges. Each prospective fit requires active charge + 1380 s + remaining check reserve ≤21600 s and CPU charge + 44160 CPU-s + remaining check reserve ≤144000 CPU-s. The larger information launch was admitted on both limits; its conditioning failure, rather than allowance exhaustion, stopped the sequence.

The information child used **49.310241 CPU-s / 49.31769729300868 wall-s** and reaped normally. Whole-command CPU is conservatively charged as 49.56 CPU-s; a separate 100 CPU-s covers static checks/reporting/commits. Program CPU is **51278.048914 + 100 + 49.56 = 51427.608914 / 144000 CPU-s**. The ledger retains all active-wall arithmetic, preparation/finish reservations and the separate 5215.0172 s historical idle interval. Numerical fit count and fit charges are zero. Executable change is **4 added / 1 removed**, giving **861/900** gross campaign lines; the bounded teardown passed cooperative and SIGTERM-resistant owned-child checks. The Engine wheel and all installed files match SHA-256 `98a140a00796782b536c892695b3546547ab5986a4905ae723190aceee38d83a`.

This evidence supports a local information diagnostic and start binary numerical verification, conditional on the fixed model, inputs and declared scales. It does not support a fitted model-form decision, independent prediction, physical validation, parameter adoption or manuscript promotion. The corrected design and its source/readiness evidence are reused without a new primary-literature claim. Delivered independent review remains with the parent; this notebook update has not been independently reviewed or promoted for manuscript use.

## Route 2b: λ=0, start A, two dielectric branches

**The larger native fit converges by function tolerance, but endpoint replay fails at Böttinger state 032 (MEA + MEAH⁺): residual 1.8575624390395507e-6 against 1e-10 after 16 iterations. There are 51 Available replay rows before the 52nd attempted row is unavailable. This is the required hard stop; derivative checks remain unrun.**

The two authorized calls use λ=0, start A, 100 iterations, 1200 s native wall and a 1320 s crash backstop, with 12000 CPU-s checked after normal reaping. Bound activity is reported. The frozen declaration has 16 coordinates and 205 positive-weight rows. CO₂–water pivot and reciprocal-temperature slope are free; all 39 Kiepe natural-log pressure residuals have weight 1/39; bicarbonate–water has upper bound 1.0. ## Default-path reproduction and Engine identity

The [fresh-process replay](results/a7-paper-evidence/default-replay/summary.json) loads the selected file through the default path and reproduces **153/153 identities**: 47 pressures (Pa), 94 species mole fractions, eight Vinjarapu integral heats (J/mol CO₂), and four Hilliard heat capacities (kJ/(kg K)). Worst relative difference is **8.39 × 10⁻¹⁶**, below $10^{-10}$. [Per-row values](results/a7-paper-evidence/default-replay/comparison.json), [input hashes](results/a7-paper-evidence/default-replay/input-hashes.json), and [timing](results/a7-paper-evidence/default-replay/command-time.json) retain the check. It took 10.99 wall-s / 10.84 CPU-s. This verifies numerical reproduction of A7 only.

The pinned Engine is merged commit `8298c6029ebb8b467929badc4a223c580ec591ab`, wheel SHA-256 `8897a0caab9f2508ed642f42c8b5226957fbe7035ed7bfdad71e4166798785b3`, with numpy 2.5.4 and scipy 1.18.1 for this replay. No Engine source checkout is imported.

Where the A7 calculations on this wheel call Ipopt, it used the MA57 linear solver. The wheel selects MA57 when the owner's licensed HSL library loads through `EPCSAFT_HSL_LIBRARY`, and MUMPS otherwise (Engine #605). The login environment has set that library since 18 October 2026, and the [A7 launcher](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/run.py.txt) passes the inherited environment to every call. The A7 result files do not store the solver; the [8298c602 transfer comparison](results/engine-8298c602-adoption/comparison.json), run on the same wheel and machine, records `ma57`. The previous pin, 21e761c3, predates that selection and used [MUMPS 5.6](results/engine-8298c602-adoption/README.md). The Engine reports MA57 and MUMPS states agreeing within about 10⁻¹¹; this repository has not compared the two solvers on A7. Acknowledgement: HSL, a collection of Fortran codes for large-scale scientific computation. <https://www.hsl.rl.ac.uk/>

CO₂ has induced 2B association with water and no self-association; its cross-association inputs are in `topology.edges` of the selected file. Ion association is absent.

Water diameter, with $T$ in K and $\sigma$ in Å:

$$\sigma_{\mathrm{H_2O}}(T)=2.78043261494+10.11 e^{-0.01775T}-1.417 e^{-0.01146T}$$

The selected file uses solvent-density-temperature permittivity with the retained shared stage-5 water parameters. It excludes dispersion between ions with the same charge sign. For MEAH⁺ and MEACOO⁻, packing diameter is 0.88 times segment diameter and Debye–Hückel diameter equals segment diameter; Born diameters vary separately. No empirical density translation is applied. Fixed and transferred inputs carry their recorded qualifications; these tables confer no new physical validation.

## Reactions

R2/R4/R5 below are generated from the current selected JSON. It does not serialize fixed R1/R3; those rows and the reaction equations come from the retained [chemistry declaration](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/blob/30ce082/data/reference/MEA/manifests/chemical_reaction_source_contract.json), including its stored aqueous-molality offsets.

::: {.parameter-table .summary-table}

| R3 · HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CO₃²⁻ + H₃O⁺ | <span class="evidence-2" title="">216.049</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">-12431.7</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">-35.4819</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">0</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">4.0165349923</span> | Fixed chemistry |
| R4 · MEACOO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + MEA | <span class="evidence-2" title="">2.151</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">-1545.3</span> | — | — | — | Selected JSON |
| R5 · MEAH⁺ + H₂O ⇌ MEA + H₃O⁺ | <span class="evidence-2" title="">3354.01716526</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">-1.28110639057</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">0.0004277</span> | — | — | Selected JSON |
:::

For R1–R3, $\ln K=A+B/T+C\ln T+DT+\Delta$; R2 already includes the conversion in $A$ and has no separate offset. For R4, $\ln K=A+B/T$. For R5, $-\log_{10}K=A/T+B+CT$. The displayed layouts therefore give $B$ in K for R1–R4 and $A$ in K for R5; $D$ for R1–R3 and $C$ for R5 are in K⁻¹. Other coefficients are dimensionless. R2/R5 include the fitted pivot-preserving enthalpy shifts at 313.15 K; R5 also varies its unshifted source A. The displayed reaction coefficients include these transformations and are not independent fitted coordinates or new source measurements.

# Pressure and speciation

The figures read A7's retained packet [pressure](results/a7-paper-evidence/pressure-figure-data.csv), [species](results/a7-paper-evidence/species-figure-data.csv), and [19 report-only Matin pool](results/a7-paper-evidence/pool-figure-data.csv) rows, derived from the single [462-row state table](results/a7-paper-evidence/state-targets.csv). # Heat of absorption

The [22 retained heat rows](results/a7-paper-evidence/heat.csv) join by record ID to `heat-rows.json`, preserving the declared scales, roles and units. Eight Vinjarapu rows at 313.15 K and 1.734 MPa enter the objective; 14 Arcis rows at 322.5 K are non-fitted predictions at their source pressures. Heat is the integral finite-addition enthalpy from zero carbon. Negative heat denotes exothermic absorption. The retained A7 assessment has no matched no-heat control.

![A7 integral heat of absorption. Open markers are observations; + markers are calculated at measured states. Vinjarapu is fitted and Arcis is a non-fitted prediction.](figures/a7_regression_overview/output/heat-of-absorption.svg){#fig-heat}

# Density and heat capacity

## Density

The [210 retained densities](results/a7-paper-evidence/density.csv) are native equation-of-state predictions, with no empirical volume translation. The objective contains 47 loaded and five CO₂-free densities. Source pressures remain the retained assumptions, including 0.100 MPa where unreported. The other retained rows preserve their non-fitted roles and exclusions.

<!-- RESULTS:density:BEGIN -->

| Source (all retained states) | n | RMSE (kg/m³) | AARD (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amundsen2009 | 103 | 6.4197 | 0.3822 |
| Hartono2014 | 40 | 2.4230 | 0.1864 |
| Han2012 | 67 | 5.9052 | 0.3924 |

<!-- RESULTS:density:END -->

**Three fitted loaded densities fail the 2s gate at 353.15 K:** `Amundsen2009_state_081` (−2.2832s), `Hartono2014_density_80C_alpha0.29` (−2.0550s), and `Hartono2014_density_80C_alpha0.39` (−2.4317s). They remain failures accepted with disclosure. Amundsen's exact source-uncertainty boundary at high temperature and loading remains unresolved (source pp. 3099–3100, locators retained per row); the density scales are not uniformly measured uncertainties. The five source-conflict Amundsen loading-0.4 rows remain excluded from the objective and gate.

## Heat capacity

The four [Hilliard Cp rows](results/a7-paper-evidence/cp.csv) enter the objective at 7 mol MEA/kg water, 101325 Pa, with the declared $10^{-6}$ unloaded CO₂ proxy. Cp uses the parameter-document molar masses for the complete analytical-feed mass, following the retained assessment conversion. The [verification record](results/a7-paper-evidence/verification.json) preserves the unloaded proxy and enthalpy checks; no new heat-capacity sweep was run.

intercept and slope both zero, T=293.15–360.25 K, source gas-free MEA mass
fractions 0.12208545–0.48838927, no reactions and neutral phase support.
It does not change the adopted parameter set discussed above.

The [retained calculation](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-4/dilute-bubble/summary.json)
compares 22 distinct states at liquid CO₂ mole fractions 1e-5, 1e-6 and 1e-7.
All 66 native partial-pressure predictions are Available with tolerance met;
the table reports the quantities supporting that conclusion.

| Quantity | Retained result |
|---|---:|
| Selected liquid CO₂ mole fraction | 1e-5 |

| Total bubble pressure / Pa | 2329.641493–57404.683320 |
| Maximum relative change of pCO₂/x to next decade | 8.75251e-5 |
| Maximum raw equilibrium residual | 1.57208e-13 |
| Cold-replay pressure change / Pa | 0 |

These scalar verification bounds are reported as a table; a plot would not
clarify the declaration check.

The [data owner](../../data/reference/MEA/physical_solubility/README.md),
Eqs.N2O-5–N2O-7, converts the 23 analogy-derived Hc values using measured
unloaded densities: Hx=Hc times gas-free total molar density. Xu Table 4
matches all 16 Xu states exactly. Hartono Table 3 requires temperature
interpolation; its 360.25 K row uses Karunarathne Table 3 measurements at
353.15 and 363.15 K. The resulting Hx range is 1.20998549e8–3.69615034e8 Pa.
Density interpolation, cross-campaign differences and analogy uncertainty
are unquantified; propagated N₂O uncertainty does not include them.

A conditional pressure estimate to 101325 Pa, using a stated 100 cm³/mol
absolute partial-molar-volume envelope, is 0.416577% for the liquid Poynting
term and at most 0.695049% including native gas-fugacity changes at fixed
bubble-vapor composition. This is below the 1% engineering threshold for that diagnostic. It does
not establish transfer from Hartono's N₂O gas reference: SI Table S2 provides
partial N₂O pressures, not the total pressure or a complete gas-fugacity
translation. Xu's actual Henry pressures and gas reference also remain
unverified because Table S3 is unread. Xu's 7.2% water-calibration discrepancy
is a separate source limitation, not a Hartono uncertainty allowance. The [evidence and limits](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-4/dilute-bubble/README.md)
retain this distinction. Start-B, derivative, dielectric-branch and exact
gas-free density checks also remain unrun. No neutral or reacting fit ran.

The density-uncertainty correction uses Karunarathne Table 3's expanded
±7.10 kg/m³ (k=2, 95% confidence); §3's ±7.80 kg/m³ applies separately to
CO₂-loaded solutions. The two retained density central values and all
historical Hc-times-density Hx values remain unchanged.

Orchestrator decision, 2026-10-16 (owner away): use Hartono SI Table S2 direct
pN₂O/xN₂O, converted by the unchanged N₂O-to-CO₂ water ratio, as the primary
Hartono Hx basis. It already uses mole fraction and needs no density
conversion. Table 11 Hc times measured gas-free total molar density exceeds
the SI ratio by 0.85368–3.09128%; retain this as a source-representation
difference, without claiming to have resolved the source volume convention.
The [derived CSV](../../data/reference/MEA/physical_solubility/CO2_physical_from_N2O.csv)
retains both source representations and selects the SI primary targets
(151298904.50–358676232.10 Pa). Their uncertainty is unquantified here;
Table 11's Hc uncertainty is not transferred to them.

Only seven Hartono observations at gas-free wMEA=0.30 and 298.35–360.25 K
are primary neutral calibration candidates, in six temperature groups.
The two 312.65 K repeats split one group weight. For repeat group g the
native log_ratio weight is 1/[6 m_g (0.05)²]; 0.05 is an engineering residual
scale. All 16 Xu rows are conditional comparisons with zero fitting weight
until Table S3 and its pressure/gas reference are verified. Preserve the

## Amendment 4: neutral CO₂–MEA pair determined; it does not change the reacting fit

**The CO₂–MEA dispersion correction is now determined independently from
neutral physical solubility, and fixing it leaves the reacting fit
unchanged.** Run 18 October 2026 on Engine `main-21e761c3`. Records:
[B1 transfer](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-4/b1-vapor-bound/README.md),
[neutral fit](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-4/neutral-fit/README.md),
[larger-d_V pair](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-4/matched-larger-dV/README.md),
[smaller-d_V pair](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-4/matched-smaller-dV/README.md).
Not yet independently reviewed as a delivered result.

**Source transfer (B1).** Hartono, Juliussen & Svendsen 2008 defines the N₂O
pressure as total minus measured solvent pressure (Eq. 5). On that basis the
N₂O vapor fugacity differs from the reported pressure by 0.37–0.60 %, and
each target carries that correction. The transfer left after it is at most
0.36–0.51 % (rows 1–6) and 0.83 % (360.25 K), inside the 1 % rule. The
source's Peng–Robinson gas balance biases its H low by 0.16–3.85 %, depending
on an unprinted fill pressure; that is a disclosed source limitation, pending
owner ratification.

**Neutral fit.** Seven Hartono 2014 rows at 30 wt % MEA, 298.35–360.25 K,
observed as the model's dilute-bubble CO₂ partial pressure at CO₂ mole
fraction 10⁻⁶. Both starts reach k(313.15 K) = 0.098720 and b = −50.989 K in
k(T) = k + b(1/T − 1/313.15 K), interior, condition 5.499, cold replay exact.
The fitted rows lie within −1.41 to +1.32 % (@fig-neutral-henry). The Xu &
Wang 2018 rows, not fitted, lie between −7.7 and +22.5 %, rising with
temperature and MEA content; near 30 wt % at 313 K they sit about 12 % above
the model while Hartono's sit within 0.5 %. The fit therefore calibrates to
one solubility campaign; transfer to other MEA contents is not shown.
b is weakly determined (local conditioning 64 K at the declared weights).

![Relative error of the model's CO₂ Henry constant at the released neutral pair. Circles are the fitted Hartono targets (30 wt %); filled markers are Xu & Wang 2018 comparison rows by MEA mass fraction. Every point is one source state; the shaded band is the falsifier's ±10 % mean-error limit.](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-4/neutral-fit/neutral-henry-errors.svg){#fig-neutral-henry}

**Matched reacting comparison.** Both arms free the same 14 coordinates on
the same 205 rows; the control fixes the CO₂–MEA pair at (0, 0) and the
variant at the neutral value.

| Branch | C166 control | C166 variant | Ratio | C149 ratio | Active bounds (both arms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| larger d_V | 39.6902 | 39.7134 | 1.00059 | 0.99999 | carbamate–MEAH⁺ k = −1; segment diameters 5.8 Å; Born diameters 5.0 Å |
| smaller d_V | 39.7366 | 39.7601 | 1.00059 | 1.00001 | the same |

The rule required C166 at least 10 % lower with the neutral pair; it is
0.06 % higher on both branches, as stated before the fits. A ratio table is
used because the result is four scalars. Cold replay (≤ 7e-12) and Kiepe
invariance (3e-15) pass in every arm. Three endpoint misses keep the decision
formally undecidable: the nine free columns have condition 3.7e4 (6.2e4 for
all 14; limit 1e4), with the weakest direction mostly on the
bicarbonate–water k_ij; the fixed-step derivative check misses at the two ion
dispersion energies by truncation (error ratio 4.0 per step halving); and
the projected gradient (0.008–0.010) is above 1e-8, although a Gauss–Newton
step would lower the cost by at most 3.6e-4. None can turn a 0.06 % increase
into a 10 % reduction. The loaded-density and per-row heat assessments were
not run at these endpoints.

**Meaning.** The five active bounds persist with or without the neutral
pair, so the CO₂–MEA interaction is not what drives the ion parameters to
their limits. This is numerical evidence on this objective, not physical
validation.

**Endpoint documents.** A campaign defect wrote R2's fitted ln K constant in
the Engine's c ln(T/T_ref) form into documents that use c ln T, 211.4 too low
(Route 2 and both Route 2b endpoint documents carry it).
The fits were unaffected; corrected documents replay cold. The same defect
caused the Route 2b endpoint-replay stop: with the constant corrected, the
Route 2b larger-d_V document replays all 205 rows to 6.7e-13.

## Amendment 6: loaded density, first density-weighted screen

**Neither evaluated amendment-4 control nor the paper record meets the loaded-density gate.** Weighting density moved the MEAH⁺ size off its bound and brought the free-column conditioning under its limit. At the unfinished endpoint the common-row cost rose 0.1 % while the Vinjarapu heat error rose from 1.52 to 1.79 kJ/mol.

Run 18 October 2026 on Engine `main-21e761c3`. Records:
[smaller-d_V densities](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/smaller-dV-density/README.md),
[density-weighted screen](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/density-sweep/README.md).
Delivered review (independent, three rounds of record corrections, no new calculation): Supported at b5d794b.

**Density at λ = 0.** The #183 gate requires each of the 20 loaded 30 wt % rows (loading up to 0.4) within 2 kg/m³. On its 12 fitted rows:
- Both A4 controls miss by −24.3 to −108.2 kg/m³. The two dielectric branches differ by at most 0.009 kg/m³.
- The paper record F1 without translation misses by +136 to +190 kg/m³ at its four retained states.
- With the empirical translation, the paper record still has 15 of the 20 gate rows outside ±2 kg/m³ (−3.68 to +3.85).
- Before amendment 6, no joint-refit fit had weighted density: every earlier retained `fit_case` has `density_weight = 0`.

**First screen: larger d_V, start A, λ = 0.01.** Here λ/12 is the weight of each density row, at scale 2 kg/m³. The fit stopped at the 100-iteration limit, so the runner refused the λ = 0.1 and λ = 1 fits until the owner decides. At that unconverged endpoint:

| | λ = 0 (A4 control) | λ = 0.01 (iteration 100) |
|---|---:|---:|
| C149 | 24.561 | 24.585 |
| Pressure / species AARD, % | 12.76 / 7.17 | 12.36 / 7.12 |
| Vinjarapu RMSE, kJ/mol | 1.52 | 1.79 |
| 12 loaded-density errors, kg/m³ | −24 to −108 | −2.9 to −24.4 |
| MEAH⁺ / carbamate segment diameter, Å | 5.8 / 5.8 | 4.47 / 5.8 |
| Free-column condition (limit 1e4) | 37,393 | 3,768 |
| Projected gradient (limit 1e-8) | 0.00812 | 0.00513 |

The table compares two endpoints across nine quantities, so a table rather than a figure.

- **Where the cost moved:** the non-density reacting cost rose 2.65 %, mostly from the corrected Jakobsen ratios (+0.86) and the Vinjarapu heats (+0.47). Pressures (−0.27) and the Matin species (−0.17) improved.
- **What stayed on bounds:** the carbamate size and both Born diameters, plus three other coordinates.
- **Shape of the remaining errors:** they grow with loading, from about −3 kg/m³ at 0.1 to about −24 kg/m³ at 0.4.
- **Checks:** the start release tests pass at λ = 0.01, 0.1 and 1 (augmented condition up to 4,887). The endpoint cold replay agrees on all 217 rows to 1.8e-12.

**Meaning.** The loaded densities add information the λ = 0 fits lacked. A small weight moves the MEAH⁺ size off its bound, cuts the loaded-density errors 4.4–8.6× row by row (mean absolute error 5.3× smaller), and brings the free-column condition under 1e4. The common-row cost rises only 0.1 % because improved pressure and species offset a worse Vinjarapu heat. The carbamate size held at 5.8 Å is one untested possible contributor to the remaining loading trend. This is numerical evidence from one unconverged fit, not a candidate or physical validation. Whether a converged fit, or a larger λ, can meet 2 kg/m³ is untested.

**Delivered, review pending; adoption withheld (phase-family gate).** The selected Held larger-dielectric-volume start-A endpoint has cost **148.2377** and reproduces **47/47 fitted loaded densities within $2s$**, with maximum absolute error **1.98$s$**. Its five CO₂-free densities pass the owner's revised **$2u=1.0$ kg/m³** gate. The same vector has **0 passed / 61 unresolved / 12 failed** phase-family points; retained split-seeded calculations confirm lower-Gibbs two-liquid states at 333.15 K and loadings 0.4 and 0.5. ### Basis, source roles and the MEA–water fit

The 19 October 2026 revision asks whether uncertainty-scaled loaded densities and the MEA–water temperature dependence can be fitted jointly while retaining the pressure, species, heat and neutral-mixture ceilings. The fitted density composition is **30 mass % MEA on a CO₂-free solvent basis**, with loading $\alpha=n_{\mathrm{CO_2}}/n_{\mathrm{MEA}}$. The principal loaded-density comparison uses Amundsen at 25–80 °C and Hartono at 20–80 °C, with assumed pressure 100000 Pa and **no empirical volume translation**. The final objective includes 15 Amundsen loaded rows, 32 Hartono loaded rows, five Amundsen CO₂-free rows, and the 50 Cai neutral-mixture rows alongside the retained reacting-property targets. The adopted propagated density scale $s$ is row-specific; $|\rho_{calc}-\rho_{obs}|\leq2s$ is not a universal ±2 kg/m³ requirement. Exact rows, source locators and scales are in the [selected density table](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-assessment/density.csv); the [assessment methods](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-assessment/README.md) distinguish exact zero-carbon, trace-carbon proxy and source-feed calculations.

The owner [removed the five Amundsen loading-0.4 rows from the objective and gate and retained Han 2012 for assessment only](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6278610430), [required joint fitting of the MEA–water pair with all 50 Cai rows](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6278891898), and [selected Held with a CO₂-free gate of $2u=1.0$ kg/m³](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6279085063). The [selected-vector assessment decision](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6279829306) withholds adoption. These decisions supersede the earlier sections' data roles and 0.5 kg/m³ CO₂-free gate for this revision only.

The retained [third-source comparison](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/source-conflict/README.md), with exact values in [third-source-values.csv](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/source-conflict/third-source-values.csv), does not resolve the source disagreement unanimously: at loading 0.4, Han's interpolated values are closer to Hartono over the shared temperatures, whereas Weiland's printed 25 °C value is closer to Amundsen. The source comparison records interpolation, preparation and uncertainty limits, including Weiland's incomplete loaded-density uncertainty. Removing five rows is an owner-selected scope change, not proof that those measurements are wrong. The excluded rows remain visible in the assessment below.

The preliminary [stage-2b fit](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/stage2b/README.md) uses

$$
k_{\mathrm{MEA,H_2O}}(T)=k_{\mathrm{MEA,H_2O}}(313.15\,\mathrm{K})+b\left(\frac{1}{T}-\frac{1}{313.15\,\mathrm{K}}\right).
$$

Here $k$ is dimensionless and $b$ is in kelvin. Both starts converge to $k=-0.0898918$, $b=-8.948$ K, with no active bound. Cai cost is 92.615 against 95.895, and CO₂-free errors at 25/40/50/70/80 °C are −0.479, −0.016, +0.023, +0.431, +0.353 kg/m³. This preliminary result is superseded by the joint fit: the selected Held document has $k=-0.08848725$ and $b=-6.268895$ K ([explicit endpoint](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/joint-mea-water/held/fit/usable-budget-endpoint.json)). Stage-2b covariance is a conditional local linearization, not measurement-propagated uncertainty for the selected endpoint.

**Bounds and stopping condition.** Six selected coordinates remain at bounds: carbamate–MEAH⁺ $k_{ij}=-1.0$; carbamate segment diameter **5.8 Å**; MEAH⁺ and carbamate Born diameters **5.0 Å each**; R5 **unshifted** $a_k=2400$ K; and R5 enthalpy shift **+10 kJ/mol**. Bicarbonate–water $k_{ij}=0.6531773314$ is **interior**, unlike the earlier candidates' +1.0 bound. The [native fit](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/joint-mea-water/held/fit/native.json), [explicit endpoint](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/joint-mea-water/held/fit/usable-budget-endpoint.json) and [chemistry coordinates](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/joint-mea-water/held/fit/chemistry-coordinates.json) distinguish the unshifted R5 coefficient from its serialized, enthalpy-adjusted value. The fit stops by relative function tolerance $10^{-6}$ at iteration 17; projected gradient 0.01334 exceeds the declared $10^{-8}$ gradient tolerance. Convergence by function tolerance and bound-active point estimates do not establish a unique optimum or uniquely identified ion properties.

**Starts and loading-basis sensitivity.** The frozen B start originally gives an Engine pre-solve refusal, `NOT_RUN: rank-deficient declared equations`, on 25 pressure rows. The [retained diagnosis](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/held-followups/diagnosis/README.md) traces this to the parameter-dependent declared-equation rank check at the Engine's generic point; it does not establish the Engine-internal cause of the rank loss. The owner authorized carbamate–MEAH⁺ $k_{ij}=-0.99$ at B's start, with the optimizer free to return to −1.0. The resulting B and smaller-branch A fits both miss Amundsen at **80 °C, $\alpha=0.3$**, by **2.11–2.12$s$**. The Hartono $x_3$ loading-basis sensitivity, starting from the selected endpoint with the frozen printed-loading density scales, gives cost **148.3398** but only **13/15 Amundsen rows within $2s$** ([declaration](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/held-followups/held-x3/fit-spec.json), [retained values](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/held-followups/held-x3/fit/native.json)). It is sensitivity evidence, not a replacement selection. The other reading of the same Hartono record, printed loading with a solvent near 30.5–30.9 mass % MEA rather than nominal 30 %, is estimated at **+0.9 to +2.3 kg/m³** and is kept separate from $s$ ([source README](../../data/reference/MEA/observations/density_viscosity/README.md), "Adopted fitting basis"); neither reading is resolved by the source.

### Gas-root and phase-family evidence

The [gas-root scratch probe](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/gas-root/run/gas-root.json) **passes** at **318.15 K, 3699.0804 Pa, $\alpha=0.25557798$**. Both native root requests return the same sole ionic root, denser than the newly solved liquid; no separate stable ionic gas root is found, and physical-solve and dilution checks complete. This is the bounded numerical probe authorized in [owner comment 6278338236](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6278338236), not evidence of global phase stability.

The phase family uses **73 unchanged design states**, a feed of **9.7292821 mol MEA + 76.9751925 mol water + $\alpha\times9.7292821$ mol CO₂**, nine-species liquid and neutral CO₂/MEA/water vapor supports, and row tolerance $10^{-10}$. The [same-driver comparison](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/phase-diagnosis/family-comparison.csv) and [diagnosis](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/phase-diagnosis/report.md) separate accepted equilibrium solutions from stability qualification:

| Parameter record | Passed | Unresolved | Failed | Points with resolved descent | Accepted final solves |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Selected Held | 0 | 61 | 12 | 12 | 73 |
| Tied joint | 0 | 59 | 14 | 14 | 73 |
| A4 larger-branch control | 0 | 73 | 0 | 0 | 73 |
| Paper declaration successor `7b0b4bb5` | 0 | 9 | 64 | 48 | 57 |

The exact older paper document `66ff7715` has 73 input-construction failures because the CO₂–MEA cross-association declaration is missing; those failures establish no phase behavior. Its existing declaration-only successor `7b0b4bb5` has **48 resolved-descent points plus 16 without an accepted final solve**, accounting for its 64 failures. Historical #172 successful-solve counts use a different wheel and solve-based rule and are not interchangeable with these stability-qualified counts.

For selected Held, all **29 resolved descending trials** admit conserved finite dense-liquid splits whose Gibbs decreases exceed their estimated numerical errors; the weakest decrease exceeds its estimate by more than $1.3\times10^5$ ([descending trials](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/phase-diagnosis/descending-trials.csv)). Split-seeded equilibrium calculations give:

| Temperature, K | Loading | Pressure, Pa | New phase state | $\Delta G/(RT)$ versus original, for the stated feed | Largest classified row residual |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 333.15 | 0.4 | 21787.8 | Two liquids | **−2.1105** | $1.64\times10^{-14}$ |
| 333.15 | 0.5 | 38286.8 | Two liquids | **−3.2496** | $3.90\times10^{-14}$ |
| 313.15 | 0.1 | 4737.14 | Two liquids + vapor | −0.01888 | $5.03\times10^{-15}$ |

Sources: [split-seeded-63.json](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/phase-diagnosis/split-seeded-63.json), [split-seeded-70.json](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/phase-diagnosis/split-seeded-70.json) and [split-seeded-21.json](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/phase-diagnosis/split-seeded-21.json). Points 63/70 compare with single liquid; point 21 compares with its original liquid–vapor state. The two-liquid changes correspond to **−5846 and −9001 J for the stated finite feed**, respectively; $\Delta G/(RT)$ is not a molar Gibbs-energy difference. These are admissible lower-Gibbs model states, not certified global minima: the new states still retain failed or indeterminate trial searches.

Zero passes also reflects a separate numerical limitation. Every selected-family point has a failed nominal-liquid, near-pure-CO₂ trial optimizer that approaches a vapor-like trace-ion state. Other tiny negative tangent-plane distances are smaller than their estimated numerical errors. The A4 control has **no resolved descent** but remains unresolved at all 73 points; its zero-pass count does not imply the selected model's dense-liquid instability. The [diagnosis report](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/phase-diagnosis/report.md) also records that no tested single parameter change removes all selected-model descents and no tested declared numerical setting earns a pass. Neither the gas-root pass nor the unresolved-trial diagnosis removes the demonstrated lower-Gibbs splits. No measured liquid–liquid separation was assessed.

### Evidence identity, uncertainty and decision limit

The selected [parameter document](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/joint-mea-water/held/fit/usable-budget-endpoint.json) has SHA-256 **`ceefc95cd051fb291e0c08675c4cb6f159bf10dca0116ef1251ba78c243f79c7`**. Its runtime mapping has SHA-256 `3018fe9aaeddab6271299d22166fa5ddce2449625a3833ec6f417d188678894d`; the phase-family summary names that mapping identity. All results above use the merged Engine commit **`21e761c318c2ac5b555a245365c844d38a93e4cb`**, wheel SHA-256 **`d2f61e3a5961b859151fbe0487f4ab633405b11620d9dd64682656a68a110357`** ([assessment provenance](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-assessment/provenance.json), [input hashes](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-assessment/input-hashes.json), [phase identities](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-checks/phase-diagnosis/provenance.json)).

The [selected numerical checks](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/selected-assessment/verification.json) reproduce the 47 fitted loaded plus five CO₂-free densities within **$1.82\times10^{-12}$ kg/m³**, heat values within **$2.97\times10^{-8}$ J/mol**, and the four mass-converted Cp values within **$10^{-10}$ kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹** of the native fit. Across 375 states, maximum stationarity, material and charge residuals are **$7.11\times10^{-13}$**, **$7.13\times10^{-13}$ mol** and **$2.27\times10^{-13}$ mol**. These finite-state replay and balance checks support numerical verification; they do not establish global stability.

The source-uncertainty scales and deterministic point estimates do not propagate parameter, source-correlation or model-form uncertainty. Bound activity, start dependence, loading-basis sensitivity and remaining source disagreements limit parameter interpretation. Non-fitted rows are conditional predictions; previously accessed rows and overlapping cohorts do not establish untouched predictive validation. The selected assessment did not perform a paired with/without-heat comparison or independently bind the complete historical #189 pure-water qualification inputs. No new pure-water sweep is inferred from this result.

The retained [program ledger](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-4/compute-ledger.json) charges **16,190 / 21,600 s** compute wall time and **127,560.61 / 200,000 CPU-s**, leaving 5,410 s and 72,439.39 CPU-s. The historical [follow-up accounting](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-6/held-followups/uncharged-compute.json) is now included once in that ledger (1,559 s / 7,317 CPU-s rounded charge); its “not yet charged” note describes the earlier handoff, not an additional pending charge. Campaign executable gross additions are **1,321 / 1,325**, under [the owner's code-ceiling decision](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6278338236). Notebook and figure preparation uses retained values only.

**Decision.** The selected Held endpoint passes the revised fitted-property gates, while the phase-family evidence prevents adoption. The unresolved trial searches and the model's resolved dense-liquid splits are distinct remaining questions. This revision is **delivered, review pending; adoption withheld (phase-family gate)**. The notebook update has not been independently reviewed or promoted for manuscript use; it does not authorize an absorber/stripper model or replacement of the currently adopted parameter record.

## Amendment 7: split-free restricted refit; three warm loaded densities disclosed

**Delivered, review pending; the owner accepted the endpoint with a disclosed loaded-density limitation.** On the qualified Engine 8298c602 wheel, a restricted refit of the same 307-row objective converges to a vector with **no resolved descent at any of the 73 family points**, where the A6 selected vector has 12 descent points. It meets every fitted-property gate except loaded density. **44/47** fitted loaded densities are within $2s$. The three misses are all at **353.15 K, α 0.29–0.39**, 4.2–5.5 kg/m³ low (0.40–0.53 %, worst **2.43$s$**). All three exceed the adopted $2s$ limits. The Hartono residuals exceed both the printed density uncertainty and the loading contributions estimated by the retained source-local secants. The Amundsen residual exceeds its adopted scale, but the source excludes the highest temperatures/loadings from its general uncertainty estimate and leaves the exact row boundary unresolved. The owner chose this disclosed density miss over A6's resolved dense-liquid splits ([#170 comment 6298116916](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6298116916)).

### Engine wheel and phase qualification

The strict gate needed a merged Engine wheel with #660. That wheel also returns equilibrium temperature and pressure as plain numbers, so the repository [adopted Engine 8298c602](results/engine-8298c602-adoption/README.md) first (previous section). The [requalification](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/fixed-study/wheel-8298c602/README.md) reran the A4 control and A6 selected families and the A6 307-row replay:

| Check | Engine 21e761c3 | Engine 8298c602 |
|---|---|---|
| A4 control family (passed / unresolved / failed) | 0 / 73 / 0 | 73 / 0 / 0 |
| A6 selected family | 0 / 61 / 12 | 61 / 0 / 12; same 29 resolved descents, \|Δ tpd/RT\| ≤ 1.1 × 10⁻¹³ |
| A6 307-row replay, max relative prediction change | | 2.1 × 10⁻¹³ |

No new descent appeared and no equation changed. The classification changes are the Engine #660 relabelling. A `no_resolved_descent` trial records that this finite trial set resolved no descent. It does not certify global stability.

### Restricted fits

The owner [chose a restricted feasibility fit](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6283335389) with MEAH⁺ segment diameter in [5.49, 5.8] Å and MEAH⁺–water $k$ in [−0.5, −0.161]. Every other box, row, scale and weight of the A6 Held declaration was kept, and the start was the screened fixed-path vector. That endpoint ([record](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/restricted/README.md)) was split-free but failed density (44/47, worst 2.70$s$) on its MEAH⁺ size bound.

Fixed-vector probes at 5.45/5.40/5.35 Å showed no resolved descent but did not pass density with size alone. The owner then approved one more fit with the size bound lowered to 5.35 Å (readiness review r1 Ready). No further fit is authorized.

The accepted endpoint ([`e234e860…`](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/restricted-2/fit/usable-budget-endpoint.json)) converged in 12 iterations, and its cold replay matches within 3.3 × 10⁻¹³. MEAH⁺ size ends on 5.35 Å, and MEAH⁺–water $k$ on −0.5. The unlike-ion $k$ (−1), the Born diameters (5 Å) and the total R5 shift (+10,000 J/mol) are on bounds as in A6. Across the warm loaded states, the split-free vectors underpredict density more than A6 does. At lower temperature both fit within the gate.

### Sensitivity, assessment and gas root

The single Hartono $x_3$ loading-basis sensitivity starts 0.002 Å inside the size bound; its moved start was screened first. It moves the parameters little: carbamate size +0.033 Å and the R2 total shift +94 J/mol. It also has no resolved descent at the 73 points. On its own basis it misses three loaded densities, worst 2.91$s$ ([record](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/restricted/README.md)).

The [full assessment](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/selected-assessment/README.md) of the accepted endpoint, against A6:

| Assessment (non-fitted rows are predictions) | A7 accepted | A6 selected |
|---|---:|---:|
| Concentration transfer, 70 states at 15/45 wt %, pressure AARD | 43.5 % | 168.7 % |
| Wagner 23 pressures AARD | 15.4 % | 20.1 % |
| Canonical 159 / 100–120 °C 54 pressure AARD | 20.6 / 24.3 % | 20.9 / 24.5 % |
| Han 2012 67 densities RMSE (assessment only) | 5.91 kg/m³ | 7.55 kg/m³ |
| Amundsen 103 densities RMSE | 6.42 kg/m³ | 4.96 kg/m³ |
| Arcis 14 heats RMSE (gate ≤ 9.36) | 8.11 kJ/mol | 8.05 kJ/mol |
| Hilliard Cp errors, 318.15 K α 0 / 0.358; 353.15 K α 0 / 0.358 | +5.53 / +2.57 / +1.15 / −2.13 % | +5.04 / +2.57 / +0.75 / −1.55 % |
| Matin 19 species pools AARD | 67.5 % | 66.8 % |

All 210 densities, 22 heats, four Cp states and 375 admitted states are available. Replays of the fitted rows agree within 1.2 × 10⁻¹¹ kg/m³. State stationarity, material and charge residuals are at most 2.2 × 10⁻¹² ([verification](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/selected-assessment/verification.json)).

The [gas-root falsifier](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/gas-root/run-2/gas-root.json) at 318.15 K, 3699.08 Pa, α 0.2556 **passes**. Its first attempt stopped at an input-path check before witness evaluation, root requests, dilution scanning and the physical solve; Engine initialization and problem compilation had already occurred. The attempt is retained and charged.

### Limits and decision

- **Phase evidence.** The phase evidence is the finite 73-point family at 313.15–333.15 K, α $10^{-5}$–0.5. It is not a stability certificate for the reacting domain.
- **Fit evidence.** Both restricted fits are single local fits from one start. They do not show that no vector passes every gate.
- **Bounds.** The lowered size bound rests on three checked vectors, not a certified box.
- **Uncertainty.** The density scales are frozen source-local loading secants. Parameter, source-correlation and model-form uncertainty are not propagated.
- **Compute.** Amendment 7 calls total 1,614.64 wall-s / 3,544.75 CPU-s ([step ledger](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/step-ledger.json)). They are charged to the program ledger at integration.

**Decision.** The owner accepted the A7 second restricted endpoint for evidence completion, with the 80 °C loaded-density miss disclosed. That evidence is now complete. The owner has now adopted it byte-identically as the [selected parameter record](results/selected-current-best-parameters.json) under [#196](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/196). The default-path replay and retained evidence package are reported in the current-record section. Delivered review of this adoption remains pending; it has not been promoted for manuscript use. It does not authorize an absorber/stripper model.
